adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsanitized URL interpolated into raw HTML footer in topic_embed.rb causes stored XSS / attribute injection

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the unescaped `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML string: `"#{url}"` and appended to `contents`. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which still allows quotes or other characters that can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute (e.g., `http://a.com' onmouseover='alert(1)`). This HTML is then stored as the post `raw` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline). That makes this a verifiable stored XSS / attribute-injection risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported content rendered as raw HTML with no HTML sanitization anywhere in the pipeline, allowing script/event handler injection from third-party feeds

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a `cook_method` that can be set to `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is where Discourse typically sanitizes HTML). `TopicEmbed.import` (used by `Jobs::PollFeed`) passes feed `contents` through `CGI.unescapeHTML(...).scrub` and `absolutize_urls`, but performs no HTML sanitization or tag/attribute filtering before creating a post with `cook_method: :raw_html`. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked`, meaning any `<script>` tags or event-handler attributes coming from the feed would be served as-is. (Note: `import_remote` uses ruby-readability with restricted tags/attributes, but the RSS/ATOM path does not.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs by rewriting them to paths on the wrong host

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, links/images are rewritten whenever href/src starts_with?('/'). Protocol-relative URLs like "//cdn.example.com/a.js" also start with '/', so they match. The code then does href.sub(/^\/+/, '') => "cdn.example.com/a.js" and rewrites to "#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/a.js" where prefix is the embed page host (e.g. "http://eviltrout.com"). That incorrectly changes an external protocol-relative URL into a path on the embed host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE in topic_retriever can permanently throttle an embed URL if the process dies between the two calls

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` as two separate commands. If the process/thread dies or an exception occurs after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` is executed, the key will be left without a TTL and will remain in Redis indefinitely, making `retrieved_recently?` return `true` forever for that `@embed_url` (permanent throttling). This is the classic non-atomic SETNX+EXPIRE issue and is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Import sha1 is updated even when the revision save fails, permanently desyncing imported content from the source

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed’s content changes (`content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`), it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. In `PostRevisor#update_post`, the code was changed to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` (non-bang) and does not check the return value. So if the post save fails (returns false) for any reason (DB constraint, callback halting save, etc.), the embed record’s `content_sha1` will still be updated, making the system believe the post content matches the source and preventing future updates—i.e., a permanent desync until manually corrected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feed items without a content element crash the whole poll run due to NoMethodError on nil.scrub
Silent retrieval failure (blank user, throttle, invalid host) causes an infinite 30-second reload loop with no diagnostics

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found it always enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `embed/loading`, whose JS reloads the page every 30 seconds indefinitely. However `TopicRetriever#retrieve` can silently do nothing in several cases: (1) `invalid_host?` returns true when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is nil/blank or when `URI(@embed_url).host` differs, (2) `retrieved_recently?` throttles via Redis, and (3) `fetch_http` returns early if `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` doesn’t map to a user (blank user). None of these paths report an error back to the controller/view, so the client can get stuck in an infinite reload loop with no diagnostics when retrieval will never succeed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Check-then-act race on import against a unique index on embed_url causes concurrent first-imports to fail

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `topic_embeds` has a unique index on `embed_url` (migration `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). But `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-act: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank it proceeds to create a post/topic and then `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)`. Two concurrent first-imports for the same URL can both observe no row and both attempt `create!`; the loser will raise due to the unique constraint (e.g., `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`). The surrounding `Topic.transaction` does not prevent this because the existence check happens before the insert and there is no locking/upsert to serialize concurrent imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Weak postMessage origin validation in embed.js uses substring check instead of origin equality
embed.js assumes the target element exists and throws if discourse-comments element is missing

adjudication.rationale: In new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then used unconditionally: `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the element with id `discourse-comments` is not present, `comments` will be `null` and this will throw a runtime `TypeError` (cannot read property 'appendChild' of null). There is no guard in the diff to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public embed endpoint enqueues unbounded retrieve_topic Sidekiq jobs for arbitrary distinct embed_url values, with no per-IP or global rate limit on job creation, creating a DoS amplification vector (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing embed is found, the code unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). There is no rate limiting at the controller level (no per-IP, per-session, or global cap) and the only throttling introduced is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which is keyed by the full `@embed_url` string (lib/topic_retriever.rb). An attacker can submit many distinct `embed_url` values (still under `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) to bypass that per-URL throttle and cause unbounded Sidekiq job creation/execution. The referer/host check does not prevent this because the `Referer` header can be spoofed by non-browser clients and only restricts the host, not the volume.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import_remote uses open(url).read with no open-uri timeout, no read size limit, and no content-type check, allowing a huge or slow remote URL to hang a worker or exhaust memory (app/models/topic_embed.rb:42-47)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` the code does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb around the added `import_remote` method). This uses `open-uri` to fetch an arbitrary remote URL and reads the entire response into memory with `.read`, but provides no `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, no maximum size limit, and no content-type validation before parsing. As a result, a slow/unresponsive server can tie up the job thread/worker, and a very large response can cause high memory usage or exhaustion. These protections are not present elsewhere in the shown method, so the risk is introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS/Atom feed on every embed-miss, turning a targeted lookup into a full-feed poll on the hot path, throttled only per-URL (lib/topic_retriever.rb:36-40)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when an embed is missing it unconditionally runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` if `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:37-40). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` fetches and parses the entire configured feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates all items importing each one (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:26-38). The only throttling in `TopicRetriever` is via `retrieved_recently?`, which keys on the specific `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so different embed URLs can each trigger a full-feed poll, turning a targeted “find this one embed_url” miss into repeated whole-feed polls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed job iterates all rss.items with no item cap, performing a per-item TopicEmbed lookup query and potentially creating thousands of topics with full PostCreator transactions per hourly run for a feed with many entries (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30-39)

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, poll_feed does `rss.items.each` with no limiting or pagination and no “last seen” cutoff. For each item it calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)`, which performs at least one DB query (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and may run a `PostCreator` transaction to create a new topic/post when the URL is new. This makes the job’s work unbounded by feed size and can be very expensive (especially on first run or if the feed contains many unique entries). The finding is grounded in the diff; while it may not create thousands of topics every hour once items are imported, it will still iterate all items and issue per-item queries each run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no read_timeout/open_timeout, so a hung feed server can indefinitely pin a worker slot, and with retry: false the scheduled job stalls (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31)

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the feed is fetched via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` using open-uri with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options. That means this scheduled Sidekiq job can block a worker thread for an unbounded/very long time if the remote server is slow or hangs during connect/read, since nothing in the code enforces a maximum duration for the HTTP fetch. The diff introduces this network call in a scheduled job context, so the availability risk is directly attributable to the change (even if the finding’s wording about “indefinitely”/“stalls” is somewhat overstated depending on Ruby defaults).

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb a method `feed_key` is added that memoizes a Redis-style key string, but it is never called anywhere in the diff (no reads/writes/use in `execute`/`poll_feed`). However, the proposed finding’s conclusion that this was meant for a conditional-GET optimization and that the job is therefore doing “redundant” work is not verifiable from the diff—polling and re-downloading the feed hourly is exactly what the job currently implements and can be an acceptable design. What is verifiable is only the presence of an unused helper method (dead code), not a correctness defect or a clearly intended but broken optimization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The embed loading page reloads the iframe every 30 seconds with no cap or backoff, polling embed/best indefinitely if the retrieve job failed (retry: false), causing repeated topic_embeds lookups and potentially enqueueing more work (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:6-10)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb the page unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds (setTimeout -> document.location.reload()). In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists for the embed_url, it always enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and renders the loading page. There is no cap/backoff/stop condition in the loading view, so if the embed never gets created (e.g., retrieval fails, invalid content, embed_by_username missing, etc.), the client will poll /embed/best indefinitely, repeatedly executing TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) and repeatedly enqueueing :retrieve_topic jobs. The retrieve job itself may early-exit due to TopicRetriever throttling, but the queueing and request/DB churn described in the finding is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook returns raw unfiltered for cook_method: raw_html, and RSS-imported content bypasses the sanitize/markdown pipeline entirely, creating a likely stored-XSS path (app/models/post.rb:131-134)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff adds `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when that cook_method is set (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). For RSS polling, `Jobs::PollFeed` takes `i.content` from the feed, does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and passes it into `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization/markdown cooking (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). As a result, feed-provided HTML is stored and then rendered verbatim (`post.cooked == post.raw`), which is a clear stored-XSS risk if the feed contains unsafe HTML/attributes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New `raw_html` cook method bypasses sanitization pipeline; externally fetched HTML from TopicEmbed.import (PollFeed RSS items, TopicRetriever/Readability fetches) is rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in embed/best.html.erb, causing stored XSS visible to anonymous users

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` for that method, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook` + plugin filters), which is where sanitization would typically occur. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` from externally supplied HTML (`contents` from RSS in `Jobs::PollFeed` via `i.content`, and from `TopicEmbed.import_remote` via Readability). Those HTML strings are stored and later displayed in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` using `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Because `post.cooked == post.raw` for `raw_html`, this renders unsanitized, externally controlled HTML, creating a stored XSS risk in the embed output (accessible without login, subject only to the referer/host check).

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError (nil.scrub) on feed items lacking a `content`/`content:encoded` element (Atom entries with only `<summary>` or RSS items with only `<description>`), and with retry: false the exception aborts the whole poll run, silently skipping remaining items
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root cause: the code calls `.scrub` on `i.content` assuming it exists, but many feeds omit `content`/`content:encoded`, causing a `NoMethodError` on nil. The candidate also notes the impact on polling and implies using summary/description as fallback, aligning with the golden fix.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage targetOrigin in embed.html.erb line 10 interpolates request.referer directly into a JS string literal without JS escaping; a referer containing a quote or `</script>` breaks out of the string/script context, enabling script execution in the Discourse origin
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same vulnerability: request.referer is interpolated into a JavaScript string without proper escaping, allowing crafted referer values (quotes/script tags) to break out of the JS context and execute arbitrary script (XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus:import CLI removes the --category/-c option, breaking existing callers/scripts that pass it (Thor rejects unknown options)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and also deletes the logic that read `options[:category]` to set `category_id`. With Thor, passing an undefined option (like `--category`/`-c`) typically raises an error for unknown switches. Therefore, existing scripts/callers that still pass `-c/--category` to `disqus:import` would break after this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus:import replaced local post creation with TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping category assignment, dropping recorded created_at for the topic post, and failing the whole import for threads with dead or non-HTTP links

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the `:category` option and all logic that looked up `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator` were removed. The old code also set `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`; the new code calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` and does not pass any `created_at`, so imported topics/posts will get the current timestamp instead of the thread’s original time. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` with no rescue; if `t[:link]` is dead/unreachable or not a supported URL, this will raise and can abort the import run (previously it didn’t fetch the remote URL at all).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js appends the iframe to `#discourse-comments` without a guard, throwing a silent JS error on host pages lacking that element

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, `comments` is assigned via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then used unconditionally: `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and this will throw a runtime `TypeError` (cannot read property 'appendChild' of null). There is no guard in the diff to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js origin check uses discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) substring matching instead of equality/prefix check, accepting postMessages from unrelated origins when the origin appears anywhere in discourseUrl's path/query
Post#cook short-circuits for raw_html before applying the public after_post_cook plugin filter hook, so plugins see inconsistent input depending on cook_method

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now returns early for raw_html posts: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. This happens before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`, so the `:after_post_cook` plugin hook is not invoked for raw_html posts. That makes plugin behavior/input/output differ depending on `cook_method`, exactly as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No timeout on outbound HTTP fetches in topic_embed.rb:44 and poll_feed.rb:33 (open-uri open().read) — jobs can hang indefinitely, exhausting Sidekiq workers on slow hosts

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces outbound HTTP fetches using open-uri without specifying any timeout options. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` it does `open(url).read`, and in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` it does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. Since no `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` (or equivalent) are provided, these Sidekiq-executed codepaths rely on library/runtime defaults and can block for an unbounded/very long time on slow/unresponsive hosts, tying up workers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No response size limit on outbound HTTP fetches, so a huge response can exhaust memory in the importing process

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple outbound HTTP fetches using `open-uri` with no size limits and then reads/parses the full body in memory. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, it does `open(url).read` and passes the entire string to `Readability::Document`, so an attacker-controlled or misbehaving remote server could return an extremely large response and cause high memory usage/OOM. Similarly, `Jobs::PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, also without any response-size cap. No safeguards (timeouts are not the same as size limits) or streaming/length checks are present in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled nil content in feed items at poll_feed.rb:37 — CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError when SimpleRSS returns nil for missing fields, aborting the entire poll

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, poll_feed iterates rss.items and does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. This unconditionally calls `scrub` on `i.content`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (common in RSS where the body may be `description`/`summary` instead), `i.content` can be nil, causing `NoMethodError` and aborting the job. There is no nil guard or fallback, so the failure is plausible and directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redis throttle in topic_retriever.rb:28-33 is non-atomic (separate SETNX and EXPIRE) — a crash between them leaves a key with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for a URL

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently? the throttle does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then, in a separate command, `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is killed after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the key will persist without a TTL. Subsequent calls will see SETNX fail and will treat the URL as "retrieved recently" forever, effectively permanently blocking retrieval for that embed_url.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race condition in TopicEmbed.import (topic_embed.rb:15-31) — concurrent imports can both pass the existence check then one fails on the unique embed_url index with no rescue/retry

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic existence check (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and then, if blank, proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). With concurrent imports of the same `url`, two workers can both observe `embed.blank?` and both attempt `create!`; the second will raise a uniqueness violation (e.g., `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`) and there is no rescue/retry/upsert logic shown in the diff, so it can blow up the job/request. This is a classic race introduced by check-then-insert with a unique constraint but no handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent failure path in embed retrieval — failures are never surfaced and the loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever with no failure detection, retry cap, or error state

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `embed/loading`. The loading template (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) unconditionally reloads the page every 30 seconds with no retry cap or error state.

If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., `TopicRetriever#retrieve` refuses to fetch because `invalid_host?` is true for the provided `embed_url`, or `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`open(url)` fails), there is no persisted failure signal and the UI will keep reloading forever while the server keeps enqueueing jobs on each reload (subject only to the retriever’s internal throttle, which still results in endless reloads). This is a verifiable behavior from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No per-item or top-level error isolation in poll_feed (poll_feed.rb:29-39) — one bad import kills the batch and the rest of the feed is silently skipped until the next hour

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `poll_feed` does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then `rss.items.each` importing each item, with no `begin/rescue` around the fetch/parse or per-item import (lines ~29-39). Any exception from network errors, RSS parsing, missing/invalid fields (e.g., `i.content`), or `TopicEmbed.import` will abort the job and stop processing remaining items. Since the job is scheduled hourly and has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a single bad item can prevent the rest of that run from importing until the next scheduled execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Resize postMessage in embed.html.erb:8 never sent when request.referer is nil — empty targetOrigin drops the message so the iframe never resizes

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb`, the `ensure_embeddable` before_filter raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` if `request.referer` is missing (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`). Therefore the embed page (and thus `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` where `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` is executed) will not render when the referer is nil. The proposed issue (“referer is nil so targetOrigin is empty and message is dropped”) does not occur on a successful response path in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer interpolation in embed.html.erb:8 is vulnerable to a referer containing a quote breaking the JS string
Missing nil/deleted-record guards: revisor.revise! in topic_embed.rb:23 may run on a nil post if deleted between import and update, raising in the scheduled job

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an embed already exists it does `post = embed.post` and then, if the content hash changed, immediately does `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)` with no guard. Since `topic_embeds.post_id` has no foreign key constraint in the new migration, the associated Post can be deleted (or the record can be otherwise missing), making `embed.post` return nil and causing a runtime error when initializing PostRevisor or calling methods on it. This can surface during scheduled feed polling or other import/update paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing deleted-topic guard in embed_controller.rb:9-11 — topic_id_for_embed can return an id for a topic deleted moments later, causing TopicView.new to raise a 500 in the user-facing iframe instead of falling back to the loading/retrieve path

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the code treats any non-nil `topic_id` from `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` as valid and immediately does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`. `topic_id_for_embed` simply plucks `topic_id` from the `topic_embeds` table with no validation that the referenced `topics` row still exists. Since the migration adds no foreign key/cascade and the model has no dependent cleanup, an orphaned `topic_embeds` row (e.g., topic deleted after embedding/import, or inconsistent data) would cause `TopicView.new` to attempt to load a missing topic and error (likely a 404/exception), and the controller would not fall back to the enqueue+loading path because `topic_id` was present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests in topic_retriever_spec.rb (lines 40-46) verify stub orchestration only, never executing the real Redis setnx/expire throttle or perform_retrieve pipeline

adjudication.rationale: The cited spec does stub internal methods: in the “valid host” context it forces `retrieved_recently?` to return true/false and only asserts whether `perform_retrieve` is invoked, without exercising the real Redis throttle (`$redis.setnx/expire`) or the actual `perform_retrieve` pipeline. However, this is a test-coverage/strategy critique rather than a concrete bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff. The code can still be correct even if these internals aren’t integration-tested here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed_spec.rb has zero coverage of the feed parsing logic, including SimpleRSS parsing, CGI.unescapeHTML, url fallback logic, and TopicEmbed.import arguments

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only asserts that execute() gates on settings and delegates to poll_feed. It never exercises Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed itself, so there is no test coverage for the newly added feed-processing logic: SimpleRSS.parse(open(...)), CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), the url fallback to i.id when i.link is blank/invalid, or that TopicEmbed.import is called with the expected (user, url, title, content) arguments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec.rb TopicView test (lines 43-47) verifies mock constructor args instead of verifying the rendered page or the posts-present branch of best.html.erb

adjudication.rationale: The cited spec does indeed only assert that `TopicView.new` is called with `(123, nil, {best: 5})` and does not exercise `best.html.erb` rendering or the `@topic_view.posts.present?` branches. However, this is a test coverage/approach critique rather than a verifiable bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff. Nothing in the diff shows the test is wrong or that behavior is broken; it’s simply a more isolated controller/unit-style test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post_revisor.rb line 85 changes @post.save to skip validations conditionally with no spec for PostRevisor#revise! with skip_validations: true or verification that the default path still validates

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. This preserves the default behavior (when `skip_validations` is nil/false, validations still run because `!nil` and `!false` are `true`) and only skips validations when explicitly requested. The proposed finding is primarily about missing test coverage, not a concrete bug or defect introduced by the change, and its claim that the default path may no longer validate is directly contradicted by the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec.rb update test (lines 42-44) doesn't assert content_sha1 is updated after re-import or that re-importing identical contents does not trigger a revision

adjudication.rationale: The cited lines in `topic_embed_spec.rb` only check that `post.cooked` contains new contents after a second `TopicEmbed.import` call. It’s true the spec does not assert `content_sha1` is updated or that identical content avoids revision, but that’s a test coverage enhancement request, not a verifiable defect/bug introduced by the diff. The implementation in `TopicEmbed.import` does update `content_sha1` on change (`embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`) and skips revision when unchanged (`if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test file exists for Jobs::RetrieveTopic; the InvalidParameters guard, user lookup, and security-relevant no_throttle/user.try(:staff?) wiring are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new job `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` with behavior worth validating (raises `Discourse::InvalidParameters` when `embed_url` missing, optionally looks up `User` by `user_id`, and passes `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` into `TopicRetriever`). The added specs cover `Jobs::PollFeed`, `TopicRetriever`, `EmbedController`, and `TopicEmbed`, but there is no new spec file targeting `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` or asserting these behaviors. So the claim that this wiring/guard logic is untested is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing edge case tests for the ensure_embeddable referer/host check: case-mismatched hosts causing spurious 403s, invalid URI referers (rescue branch never exercised), and the integration gap between the controller check and TopicRetriever#invalid_host? that can strand users on a permanent loading page
embed.js postMessage origin check uses substring matching (indexOf) and has zero tests; the resize-postMessage sender in embed.html.erb posting to the raw referer is also untested
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate notes that the resize postMessage sender is posting to the raw referer, which aligns with the golden issue that targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port) rather than the full referrer URL. Although it also mentions substring origin checking and missing tests, it still identifies the same underlying targetOrigin/referrer misuse.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed's silent-return path when embed_by_username doesn't match an existing user (and the same pattern in TopicRetriever#fetch_http) is untested, leaving the common misconfiguration case with no signal

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, if `embed_by_username` is set but no matching `User` exists, it does `return if user.blank?` without logging or raising. The same silent no-op exists in `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (`return if user.blank?`). The added specs only test that `execute` requires `embed_by_username` to be present, not the misconfiguration case where it is present but invalid, and there are no tests covering `fetch_http`’s early return either. This leaves a likely misconfiguration producing no work and no signal, and that branch is currently untested in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw HTML posts (cook_method == raw_html) skip sanitization/rendering pipeline; PollFeed passes unescaped feed HTML into TopicEmbed.import stored with skip_validations and rendered via raw, creating a stored XSS path from malicious feed content with no tag whitelist gate like import_remote has

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html`, and `Post#cook` now returns `raw` immediately when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook` + filters). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts via `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`, so the stored post content is rendered verbatim. `Jobs::PollFeed` pulls `i.content` from `SimpleRSS.parse(open(feed_url))`, does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import` with no whitelist/sanitization step (unlike `import_remote`, which uses `Readability::Document` with explicit allowed tags/attributes). As a result, malicious HTML/JS in the feed can be stored and later emitted as-is (e.g., via `raw post.cooked` in the new embed view), creating a stored XSS path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor's skip_validations option changes semantics of a shared code path — any caller passing skip_validations silently bypasses all post validations on revision; embed concern should stay in TopicEmbed

adjudication.rationale: The diff deliberately changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. This means callers can now explicitly bypass validations by passing `skip_validations: true`—and the new embed/import code does exactly that (`revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`). That is a semantics change, but it is not a verifiable defect in the diff: the option name matches the behavior, and there’s no evidence in the diff of unintended callers relying on `skip_validations` for something else or being impacted. The “embed concern should stay in TopicEmbed” part is architectural preference, not a concrete bug/security issue demonstrated by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever synchronously invokes Jobs::PollFeed.execute inline, a layering violation bypassing job infrastructure (retry semantics, recurrence guard) and running synchronously inside a web request; feed-polling logic should be extracted into a reusable service

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, when feed polling is enabled it directly runs the scheduled job inline: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`. This bypasses the job infrastructure (it is not enqueued/scheduled by Sidekiq/Jobs) and ignores the job’s intended recurrence (`recurrence { hourly }`) and options (`sidekiq_options retry: false`). It also means the entire feed is fetched/parsed as part of the TopicRetriever execution path (triggered by the retrieve_topic job), which can cause unexpected extra work and defeats the “scheduled hourly poll” design.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated embed author user lookup logic in poll_feed.rb and topic_retriever.rb, and duplicated URL scheme guard across topic_embed.rb and poll_feed.rb — domain rules in three places will drift; should be consolidated in TopicEmbed

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show duplicated logic: both `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` and `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` look up the embedding user via `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first`, and both `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` and `TopicEmbed.import` contain URL scheme checks. However, this is a maintainability/refactoring concern (potential future drift), not a clear bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff. The current duplicates are consistent and do not demonstrably cause incorrect behavior in the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed model is a grab-bag fusing HTTP fetching, HTML rewriting/whitelist policy, I18n copy injection into stored content, and persistence orchestration; also mutates the caller's contents string via contents << side effect

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, title, contents)` which does `contents << "\n<hr>..."`, mutating the String object passed by the caller (Ruby passes object references). That side effect is directly verifiable in the code and could lead to unexpected behavior if the caller reuses `contents` after calling `import`. The rest of the finding (model combining fetching/parsing/rewriting/persistence) is more of a design critique, but the mutation is a concrete correctness concern introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed assumes every feed item has content and usable link/id — a malformed item (no content, only summary/description) raises NoMethodError and, with retry: false, silently aborts the entire poll; non-HTTP urn:/tag: ids are silently dropped

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, each item does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is `nil` (common for feeds that only provide `summary`/`description`), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, which would abort processing of the rest of the feed. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so it won’t be retried automatically. Also, URL selection does `url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`, but `TopicEmbed.import` immediately returns unless the URL matches `^https?://`; so if `link` is blank/non-http and `id` is a non-HTTP URN/tag, the item is silently skipped (import returns `nil`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead locale key: embed.permalink is added but never referenced anywhere in the code

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed.permalink` under `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and within the changed/added files in this diff the embed-related views/models reference `embed.title`, `embed.start_discussion`, `embed.continue`, `embed.loading`, and `embed.imported_from`, but not `embed.permalink`. However, the claim that it is "never referenced anywhere in the code" cannot be verified from the diff alone (there could be references in unchanged files), and an unused locale key is not a clear correctness/security defect—more of a cleanup/nit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js origin check uses substring indexOf instead of origin equality, allowing origins containing the discourse URL as substring (e.g. http://discourse.example.com.attacker.io) to forge resize messages; should compare parsed origin
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying vulnerability: validating postMessage/event origin with a substring/indexOf check can be bypassed by attacker-controlled domains that include the trusted discourse URL as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com / discourse.example.com.attacker.io). The candidate also suggests proper origin parsing/equality, aligning with the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated changes mixed into the PR: force: true added to an already-released migration risks dropping top_topics data on replay, and migrate_word_counts.rb contains whitespace-only churn

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which introduces a concrete data-loss risk if that migration is ever replayed against a DB that already has `top_topics` (e.g., during a reset/re-run scenario). The diff also shows whitespace-only churn in `20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` (trailing whitespace removal / newline changes), which is unrelated to the embedding feature change and adds noise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook's raw-html early return bypasses the :after_post_cook plugin filter, creating an invisible behavioral fork for plugins registered against that hook

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now does `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` before calling `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. This means posts using the new `:raw_html` cook_method (set during TopicEmbed.import via PostCreator with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`) will never trigger the `:after_post_cook` plugin hook, unlike regular posts. That is a concrete behavioral divergence introduced by the diff and can break plugins that rely on that hook to post-process cooked content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs (//cdn.example.com/x.js) by prefixing the origin, breaking them; should exclude //-prefixed values or use URI.join

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both `href` and `src` are rewritten whenever the value `start_with?('/')`. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.js` (or `//cdn.example.com/img.png`) also start with `/`, so they will be transformed into `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`, yielding something like `http://origin/cdn.example.com/x.js`, which is incorrect and breaks the URL. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: PollFeed passes unsanitized feed content to TopicEmbed.import with cook_method raw_html, which is rendered verbatim via raw post.cooked, allowing script/event-handler payloads from third-party feeds to execute

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed, the code takes `i.content` from the parsed feed (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import(...)` without any sanitization/whitelisting. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` verbatim for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders this via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any `<script>` tags or event-handler attributes (e.g., `onerror`) present in the feed content would be stored and rendered as active HTML/JS. This is a verifiable stored XSS vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb interpolates raw URL directly into an HTML attribute (<a href='#{url}'>), allowing crafted URL paths to break out of the attribute

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb, TopicEmbed.import appends HTML to `contents` using string interpolation: `"#{url}"` inside the `embed.imported_from` translation. The only validation on `url` is a regex `^https?\:\/\/`, which does not prevent quotes or other characters that can terminate the single-quoted href attribute. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, Post#cook returns `raw` (bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline), and the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore a crafted URL containing `'` (or similar) could break out of the attribute and inject HTML/JS, making this a real, diff-introduced XSS issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :top_topics, force: true edit in already-shipped migration 20131223171005 will silently drop and recreate top_topics on environments that re-execute it, destroying cached ranking data

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it, rather than raising an error. If this migration is ever re-executed on a DB that already has `top_topics` (e.g., via rollback/re-run, db:migrate:reset, or any scenario where migrations are replayed against an existing schema), it can silently destroy the existing `top_topics` data. This is a real risk introduced by the diff; without `force: true` it would fail loudly instead of dropping data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed crashes on feeds without <content>: SimpleRSS returns nil for missing content field, so nil.scrub raises NoMethodError, and with retry: false the entire polling run fails silently, permanently breaking feed import

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. `SimpleRSS.parse` items may not have a `content` field (many RSS feeds use `description` or other fields), in which case `i.content` can be `nil`, and calling `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the polling run. The claim about it "permanently" breaking is overstated (it will keep failing on each run until the feed or code changes), but the underlying crash on missing `<content>` is a real defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: String#scrub requires Ruby 2.1+ but the codebase targets Ruby 2.0, so scrub raises NoMethodError for every feed item and feed polling never works on the stated platform

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`. While `String#scrub` is only available in newer Ruby versions (and would raise `NoMethodError` on older Rubies), the claim that “the codebase targets Ruby 2.0” is not established anywhere in the provided diff (no `.ruby-version`, Gemfile ruby directive, etc.). Therefore the incompatibility is conditional/speculative based on external assumptions about the supported Ruby version, and cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false rewrites the entire posts table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PostgreSQL < 11, blocking all reads/writes during migration on large datasets

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` with `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-NULL DEFAULT forces a table rewrite and requires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the table for the duration of the rewrite, which can block reads/writes on a large `posts` table during deployment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true on brand-new topic_embeds table (20131217174004) is a destructive guard-rail removal; if the migration runs twice due to partial-failure recovery, already-imported rows are silently destroyed

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` does include `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which would drop/recreate the table if it already exists. However, in normal Rails operation migrations are not run twice (tracked in `schema_migrations`), and on common DBs like PostgreSQL the `change` block DDL runs inside a transaction so a failure would roll back the table creation rather than leaving a partially-created table to be rerun. The proposed scenario (“migration runs twice due to partial-failure recovery” and “already-imported rows are silently destroyed”) is not directly supported by anything in the diff (this migration itself does no importing), and requires atypical/manual rerun conditions. So this is more speculative risk than a verifiable problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever's $redis.setnx followed by separate non-atomic $redis.expire can leak the throttle key permanently if the process dies between calls, permanently blocking retrieval of that embed URL for non-staff users

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two distinct Redis commands; if the process/thread dies or raises between them, the key can be created without a TTL and will then cause subsequent calls (where `setnx` returns false) to treat it as “retrieved recently” indefinitely for non-staff users. This matches the finding and is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: raw_html cook path returns raw verbatim with no sanitization anywhere in the pipeline; attacker-controlled RSS HTML from PollFeed is stored and rendered via '<%= raw post.cooked %>' on embed and main topic pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with a `:raw_html` option, and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true` using `contents` sourced from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly) or fetched HTML via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. The embed view renders `post.cooked` using `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Since the cooking step for these posts returns the raw HTML without sanitization, attacker-controlled HTML from the feed/page can be stored and rendered, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML attribute injection in TopicEmbed.import footer: url is interpolated unescaped into a single-quoted href attribute, allowing stored XSS via crafted URLs that pass the /^https?\:\/\// check

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the footer HTML is constructed with string interpolation: `"#{url}"` and appended to `contents`. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which only checks the prefix and does not prevent quotes or other characters. A crafted URL like `http://example.com' onmouseover='alert(1)` would pass the regex and break out of the single-quoted href attribute, injecting arbitrary attributes/HTML. This content is then stored and later rendered as raw HTML because imported posts set `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly, and the embed view uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, making this a stored XSS vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed crashes on feed items missing 'content' (NoMethodError on i.content.scrub); with retry: false and no per-item rescue, the exception aborts rss.items.each mid-loop and every subsequent hourly run fails at the same item, silently preventing all later items from ever importing

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, each item does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is `nil` (common for many RSS feeds that use `description`/`summary` instead of `content`), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire `rss.items.each` loop with no per-item rescue. Since the job is scheduled hourly and has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, it won’t retry immediately, and the next hourly run will hit the same bad item again and fail before importing later items (assuming the problematic item remains present/early in the feed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Main Gemfile.lock not updated after adding ruby-readability and simple-rss (only Gemfile_rails4.lock modified), so the default Rails 3 bundle will fail with 'could not find gem'

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` to `Gemfile`, but only updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock`. There is no corresponding update to the primary lockfile (typically `Gemfile.lock`) in this change, so any bundle that relies on the main lockfile would have an out-of-sync lock and can fail to resolve these new dependencies until that lockfile is updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ensure_embeddable guard uses client-forged Referer header to authorize embeddable hosts, allowing anonymous users to render any topic's posts on /embed/best and trigger server-side URL fetching via Jobs::RetrieveTopic

Non-atomic redis setnx/expire in TopicRetriever: if the process dies between setnx and expire, the key persists with no TTL, permanently throttling that embed_url and leaving the loading page reloading every 30 seconds forever; should use SET key val NX EX 60

adjudication.rationale:
In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `retrieved_recently?` throttling is implemented as:

```ruby
if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
  $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
  return false
end
true
```

Because `SETNX` and `EXPIRE` are two separate commands, if the process crashes or is interrupted after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without a TTL. On subsequent calls `setnx` will always fail and the method will always return `true` (throttled), preventing `perform_retrieve` indefinitely for that `@embed_url`. This matches the proposed finding and is a real correctness/availability risk introduced by the diff; using `SET ... NX EX 60` (or a transaction/Lua script) would make it atomic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded job-churn loop: every embed page view enqueues a RetrieveTopic job and the loading page auto-reloads every 30 seconds forever with no backoff, amplifying load against Sidekiq and the DB when retrieval keeps failing

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing `topic_id` is found, it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. The `loading.html.erb` view then reloads the page every 30 seconds indefinitely. If retrieval keeps failing (e.g., remote fetch errors, missing user, bad settings), each reload repeats the controller action and enqueues another `RetrieveTopic` job. Although `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles the *work* (via a 60s Redis key) and `perform_retrieve` bails if an embed already exists, there is no throttle/deduplication on the enqueue itself, so Sidekiq can still accumulate and execute a steady stream of mostly-noop jobs plus repeated DB/Redis checks, indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Check-then-create race in TopicEmbed.import: concurrent imports of the same URL can both pass the where().first check, causing the loser to raise RecordNotUnique from the unique index unhandled after wasting work, with no rescue/retry

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to create a post and then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. Because there is a unique DB index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (added in `CreateTopicEmbeds`), two concurrent imports of the same `url` can both observe no existing row and both attempt `create!`; the second will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or equivalent) and there is no rescue/retry. This is a classic check-then-insert race that is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: skip_validations in PostRevisor silently disables validation for all revise! callers passing the flag, letting posts that would fail normal validation (e.g., length limits) be persisted and rendered everywhere

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, enabling an explicit opt-out of validations when `skip_validations: true` is passed. In this same diff, `TopicEmbed.import` calls `revise!` with `skip_validations: true` to update embedded/imported posts. This is an intentional behavior change to honor a flag already being supplied, not an accidental “silent” disabling affecting normal callers. The finding describes a general risk of skipping validations, but the diff does not show an unintended or incorrect use—it's an explicit, opt-in path used for imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js origin check uses discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 instead of exact equality, accepting any origin that appears as a substring within discourseUrl

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler does `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is not an exact origin comparison; it accepts any `e.origin` that appears as a substring anywhere inside `discourseUrl`. A correct `postMessage` origin check should compare origins exactly (e.g., against the expected Discourse origin), not via substring containment, because containment can be bypassed in cases where the expected origin string appears within a different URL/host string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed --category/-c option from disqus:import task breaks existing automation with Thor 'unknown option' errors, and the switch to import_remote performs thousands of synchronous HTTP fetches importing current page content instead of archived Disqus content

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, so any existing automation invoking `disqus:import -c/--category` will now fail with Thor “unknown option” errors. The diff also changes the import behavior from creating the topic locally with a simple permalink raw (`PostCreator.new(... raw: "[[Permalink](...)]" ...)`) to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, which in turn does `open(url).read` and parses it via `ruby-readability`. That introduces a synchronous HTTP fetch per imported thread and imports whatever the page currently serves, which is a concrete behavioral change visible in the code.
